name: Spaceship
description: A fully themed starship crew where everyone talks ship, from the bridge to the galley, in cool deck greys and teal under a field of stars.

bossVisit: Morning, crew. Best orbit yet, please.
My door is always open. Mind the pressure seal.
Figures before we pass the moon again, please.
Just a quick sync. Ship quick, so about an hour.
Splendid. Take the orbit off. Not literally.
Briefing room. The chairs are bolted down.
Is that a star chart or a spreadsheet?
Lovely telemetry. Which way is up?
Keep those thrusters happy!
Report! Briefly. Very briefly.
That console has never looked so busy.
Excellent. Log it, then log that you logged it.
Are we still going the right way? Good.
Whatever that is, do more of it.
Superb. I'll tell ground it was my idea.
Smashing progress. Don't smash anything.
Deadlines look small from here. They aren't.
Is this the bit where we go faster?
Good. Very good. Is it meant to beep?
Keep it up. Up is the way we're facing.
Next sunrise in five minutes. Impress me.
That graph goes all the way to the stars.
Carry on. I'm only the captain.
Brilliant. Done by the next orbit?
Lovely. Double-check the airlock, though.
Don't mind me. Just inspecting the inspecting.
Mission goals! Love them. What are ours?
Morale looks high. Is the gravity on?
Fine work. The vacuum outside is jealous.
Fine flying. Well, fine typing.
bossSnack: Freeze-dried cake has no calories. Science.
Low gravity. It barely weighs anything.
I'm the captain. This is a ration.
One for me, one for crew morale.
It's for the long-haul stretch. Which is now.
Pudding in a pouch counts as water.
A captain must test the supplies. Thoroughly.
Two flapjacks. In case of meteor.
The bridge runs on biscuits. Ask anyone.
It's in a tube. Tubes are healthy.
Emergency rations. The emergency is lunch.
bossSnoop: Carry on. Pretend I'm a porthole.
No mistakes, please. Space is unforgiving.
bossSulkStart: Take the ready room. I'll just float about.
Mind the chair. It swivels to starboard.
The view's lovely. You'll hate it.
Fine. Relieved of command. For a bit.
Don't touch the big red button. Or do.
Water the fern. It came from home.
Enjoy my porthole. It's mine, really.
Very well. I shall command the corridor.
Wipe your boots. That rug is vacuum-sealed.
The intercom button sticks. Good luck.
bossSulk: It's not even the best porthole.
This corridor has no captain's chair.
Even the airlock gets more respect.
Nobody salutes a captain in a corridor.
This tea tastes of exile and recycler.
I'll count stars. One. Two. Plenty.
My chair is probably spinning without me.
bossSulkEnd: Right. Shift's over. Out of my chair.
Command restored. Thank you, that'll be all.
The fern missed me. I can tell.
Back on the bridge. Well, the room.
Ah. The chair still knows my shape.
Captain on deck! It's me. I'm the captain.
Lovely. Nobody touched the button. Did they?
Normal service resumes. Mind the door.
Thank you for your service. Please leave.
deskBumped: I had the console set just right.
Off to the back of the ship, then.
I'd only just warmed the seat. In space!
Bumped by a higher rank. Classic.
I'll take my mug. It's magnetic. It's mine.
Fine. Someone else can watch the asteroids.
Packing my one sock and a star chart.
deskMoveUp: Ooh, a console with a view.
I can see the moon from here!
Shiny buttons. I won't press them. Yet.
Look at me, right by the bridge.
I shall try not to gloat in zero g.
Upgraded. My console beeps in a major key.
Front row for the stars. Lovely.
chatReplies: Most ship thing I've heard all day.
Say that slower. I'm low on oxygen.
I'll put it in the ship's log.
That explains the noise from deck six.
Funny. My console said the same.
We've all been there. We're all still here.
Steady. We're a long way from home.
No argument from me. Or the moon.
Don't. I'll laugh into my helmet.
Wise words for a Tuesday in orbit.
Sounds about right, for out here.
Huh. Never thought of it like that.
receptionPhone: Larkspur comms desk, go ahead.
Comms. Go ahead, I'm listening.
Ground control? You're breaking up. Good.
A delivery? Dock it round the side.
Sorry, who's hailing?
You're through to deck nine. Mind the echo.
No, we can't pull over.
Signal's weak. Try standing nearer a star.
The captain's in a briefing. With a biscuit.
Wrong ship. Easy mistake out here.
Please hold. The hold music is the reactor.
Message received. Slightly scorched.
A shuttle asking for parking. Again.
Can I take a message? I'll float it over.
Hello? Static. Rude static.
You want the cargo hold. Transferring.
Ground says hello. Ground always does.
Solar flare on the line. Call back later.
Incoming hail! Oh. It's the kettle.
Is this about the moon parking fine?
Still in orbit, yes. No, we can't wave.
Space weather update? Lovely. Go on.
Hydroponics? It's the seed supplier again.
Lift engineer. Fourth time this week.
Spell that slowly, please. There's a lag.
Your shuttle's late. It sends apologies.
receptionGreeting: Welcome aboard! Wait for the green light.
Wipe your boots. Moon dust gets everywhere.
Badges on the left. Left has the window.
Inner door first, then outer. Never reversed.
Fresh crew! Your locker is the one that hums.
Hello! Pressure's equal. Step on out.
There you are. Lift took the scenic route?
Welcome aboard. Mind the gravity step.
New face! Grab a suit. They're one size.
Good orbit! Coffee's in the galley.
Ah, a new crewmate. Mind your head.
Welcome! Your sleep pod is nearly made.
receptionIdle: Somebody ordered nine hundred airlock seals.
The radar blipped. It was a crumb.
Logbook's up to date. I logged that too.
Signal: one bar. Mood: two bars.
Another sunrise. That's eleven today.
Note to self: stop waving at satellites.
The dish needs a dust. From outside.
The lift is doing its countdown again.
If I lean left, I can see the moon.
Parcel for hydroponics. It's wriggling.
Static. Lovely, soothing static.
Filed the shuttle times under 'optimism'.
Three hails, two wrong numbers, one comet.
My headset smells of reactor.
Three clocks, three time zones, no lunch.
Visitor log: one moth. How, though?
Ground sent a smiley face. I'm framing it.
The intercom crackles when it's happy.
Docking slot says Tuesday. Which Tuesday?
Someone's left a helmet on the sofa.
I could alphabetise the stars. Or not.
Comms are quiet. Suspiciously quiet.
Outer door's sealed. Inner door's sulking.
Is that a comet or a smudge on the glass?
Ninety-minute days. Eight-hour shifts. Maths.
receptionAttending: Orders? I'll patch them straight through.
Comms ready. What are we changing?
cleanerMutters: Crumbs in zero g. They get everywhere.
Moon dust. Always moon dust.
Off they go. I'll wipe their console, shall I.
Who floats a teabag into the vent?
Nose prints on the porthole. Again.
Bin's full of foil pouches. Again.
Sticky. Why is the joystick sticky?
One more airlock to mop. Just the one.
I polish the hand rails. Nobody notices.
Spilled soup on the ceiling. Classic.
Somebody's left a sock in the recycler.
Galley counter's done. Don't breathe on it.
That's not dust. That's a small nebula.
Desk's free. Wipe, polish, salute.
Gloves on. Bucket on. Standards on.
The vacuum outside is cleaner than this.
Ice crystals in the bin. Lovely.
The scrubbers can't scrub this. I can.
Every deck, every day. Nine decks.
Floating hair in the shower. Floating!
Quiet shift. Just me and the hum.
Coffee ring on the star chart. Tsk.
My bucket has a lid now. Lesson learned.
Mopping in low gravity is just dancing.
Left their mug. It's growing a garden.
Tidy console, tidy course. That's my motto.
cartCalls: Galley cart coming through!
Soup in a tube! Hot soup in a tube!
Freeze-dried ice cream! Still crunchy!
Tea? Course you want tea. It's space.
Hydroponic salad! Grown three decks down!
Rehydrated stew! Just add water and hope!
Mind your feet! The cart has no brakes!
Crater cakes! Lumpy on purpose!
Fresh bread! Fresh-ish! Bread-ish!
Hot drinks with lids! Mandatory lids!
Tomato soup! The tomatoes had names!
Biscuits that don't crumble! Mostly!
Last call before the next sunrise!
Algae crisps! Better than they sound!
Sandwiches, strapped down for freshness!
Coffee strong enough to change orbit!
Pudding cups! Pressure-tested!
Noodles! They float, you slurp!
Curry! Clears the sinuses, fogs the visor!
Fruit cups! Real fruit, from a real planet!
Ration bars! Beige, tan or oat!
Cart's parked. Form an orderly orbit.
Hot chocolate! Floating marshmallows extra!
Cheese on toast! Toasted by actual sunlight!
Buy two pouches, get a free straw!
Nice and warm! Like a reactor, but tasty!
itFix: Right. Let's vent it and repressurise.
itVerdicts: It was the coupling. It's always the coupling.
Rerouted the power. Don't ask where from.
Fixed. Please never hail us again.
Ticket closed. Sealed, like an airlock.
Gave it a kick. Ship-standard procedure.
Cleared the buffer. Whatever that is.
That'll hold till the next asteroid.
Dust in the vents. Mostly space dust.
Back up. I'm logging that as heroism.
Working. I'm off to stare at a bulkhead.
Done. Someone tell the captain I'm brilliant.
itGiveUps: Gone? Fine. I'll leave it rebooting.
Talking to an empty chair. In space.
Off to the galley, I bet. Smart.
Right. I was never on this deck.
Can't fix what's left the room.
Abandoned, like an old probe. Lovely.
itSneers: It wrote the docking checklist as a poem.
Six em dashes in one flight log. Six.
It said 'delve'. Into a fuel report.
Bold text everywhere. Even on the oxygen.
A summary of the summary of the orbit.
'Great question!' It was a pressure reading.
It invented a planet. A whole planet.
It plotted a course in bullet points.
Forty lines of code to open one airlock.
It says it ran the tests. In vacuum? No.
It wrote a mission statement for a fuse.
itComebacks: That was my whole flight plan.
You rebooted me into the wrong decade.
Where was I? Which deck am I on?
I was about to dock that thought.
I feel lighter. Is the gravity off?
Hello. Who am I? Who's flying?
I shall start again. From launch.
itFixerMutters: Nobody ever thanks the systems crew.
If I walk slowly, I fix fewer things.
Should have stayed in the server bay.
I'm not lazy. I'm conserving oxygen.
Is that a beep? Not my beep.
Engine room's warm. I miss it.
Ticket four hundred. On a crew of forty.
Someone's wiggled a cable. I can feel it.
If it's floating, it's not my department.
I could fix the lift. Or I could not.
itCriticMutters: Fourteen alarms. All amber. Oh dear.
I counted the rivets. Nine hundred and six.
Someone microwaved fish. In a sealed hull.
Is that hiss normal? Please be normal.
The airlock log has a typo. I can't rest.
The stars aren't aligned. I checked.
The hand rails are sticky. I made a note.
My crib card has a coffee ring. Devastating.
Gravity is at ninety-nine per cent. Why?
Fire drill at three. I've practised twice.
I double-checked the hatch. Triple, now.
itTalkReplies: You've lost me. And the signal.
Could you say that slower, in metric?
That's not how space works. Is it?
itFixerTalk: Nice vacuum out there today.
Very empty. That's how I like it.
Talking to people. Bit much, isn't it?
Right. That's my quota till next orbit.
Cold on deck three. Good for cables.
Every deck is good for cables.
Ever just stare into the void?
It doesn't stare back. Unlike the captain.
The lift and I aren't speaking.
It started it. With the countdown.
Fancy a look at the reactor? No? Fair.
It's just a big kettle. A very big kettle.
Me? I'm on a break. Since launch.
Long launch. Very long launch.
Did you hear the hull creak earlier?
That was me. Bad knees.
Asteroid belt next week. Should be fun.
Fun for the rocks, anyway.
Server bay's the comfiest room aboard.
Don't tell anyone. I've got a hammock.
Ever wonder what's beyond the stars?
More cables, probably.
itCriticTalk: Solar wind's backing westerly, I hear.
No west in space. The card says there is.
Lovely orbit we're having. For an ellipse.
That was a compliment. To the ellipse.
How about those comets? Very... tailed.
The card says 'tailed'. I said it.
Shocking state of the asteroid league.
I do not know what an asteroid league is.
Has the moon had a haircut?
Card says it's a joke. I laughed early.
Big gravity this week. Heavy stuff.
That was the pun. The card has one pun.
How's the family? Your crew family?
Card says crew are family. Alarming.
Docking season, eh? Rough on the knees.
I have never docked. I have read about it.
Did you catch the meteor shower? Damp?
Meteors are not damp. I see that now.
The nebula's looking peaky this season.
Peaky. Who wrote this card?
What's your sign? Mine is the hatch.
The hatch symbol. It's a very good sign.

smallTalk: Is the lift to deck four working today?
It works. It just insists on a countdown.
Has anyone seen my magnetic mug?
It's stuck to the fridge. They've made friends.
Who keeps setting the corridor lights to sunset?
Facilities. Says it lifts morale eight per cent.
How was shore leave?
Lovely. Rain is wild. Water just falls down.
The recycler made the coffee taste of carrots.
Then it's a carrot day. Lean into it.
Coming to the docking drill this afternoon?
Only if there are biscuits at the muster point.
What's that humming noise?
Engines or the fridge. They've been competing.
Fancy a walk round the ring at lunch?
Go on. It's one lap, but it's a long one.
Sleep well?
The pod was fine. My feet drifted off first.
Is gravity a bit strong today?
No. You had two puddings.
Which shift are you on?
The one where the sun rises sixteen times.
Did you see the ocean go by?
Twice. I waved both times.
Anyone for a game of cards?
Last time the deck floated into the vent.
Hydroponics smells amazing today.
They've grown mint. Everyone's very excited.
Who left the airlock on manual?
Nobody. That's what worries me.
How's the view from your bunk?
A wall. A very nice wall.
Space weather forecast?
Sunny, with a chance of solar flare.
Is the cargo hold always this cold?
Only on days ending in y.
Have you done your suit check?
My suit checked me. I failed.
I think I left my toothbrush floating.
Check the vent. It all ends up there.
Fire drill at two?
Two ship time or two home time?
Did the shower work for you?
It's less a shower and more a cloud.
I miss proper bread.
Bread makes crumbs. Crumbs are banned.
Where does our water come from?
Don't ask. Just drink it confidently.
Heard the meteor shower was lovely.
Lovely from inside. Noisy on the hull.
Anyone know the time back home?
Tea time. It's always tea time somewhere.
Why is there a sock on the ceiling?
Laundry day in zero g. Look up more.
The exercise bike is free.
It's been free since launch. Nobody wants it.
Ground sent me a birthday card.
Lovely. Did it arrive before the birthday?
Is coffee rationed now?
No. Just the queue for it.
What's in the unlabelled crate?
Spare filters. And forty jars of jam.
Did you hear that clunk?
Docking clamp. Or the kettle. Same noise.
Who's on hull inspection today?
Me. I've packed sandwiches and courage.
How do you sleep with all these sunrises?
Eye mask. Two eye masks.
The salt comes as a liquid here.
So does the pepper. Pepper drops are wild.
Can you see home from the observation deck?
On a clear day. It's always a clear day.
Quiz night is tomorrow.
Last time every answer was 'oxygen'.
Is there any post today?
One parcel. It's been in orbit for weeks.
My hair's gone all floaty.
Very fashionable on deck six.
Did you pass your spacewalk test?
I passed. My lunch didn't.
Why does the galley smell of toast?
The toaster's back. Long story. Small fire.
Who's been talking to the plants?
Everyone. Best listeners aboard.
Is that satellite still following us?
I wave at it every morning. It's polite.
The oxygen tastes fresher today.
Filter change. It tastes of new filter.
How's your sleep pod?
Snug. Like a sock with opinions.
Have you seen the comet?
Seen it, named it, been told off for naming it.
We're slowing down, aren't we?
Only for lunch. Even ships need lunch.
My boots keep sticking to the floor.
Magnetic soles. Or the galley spill.
Film night is a space film again.
Bold choice. Very relatable.
Did the captain say anything about leave?
Something about 'next orbit'. Every orbit.
What's for dinner?
Something beige, so probably stew.
Why is the corridor so long?
It's a ring. It just keeps going.
Any news from home?
It rained. Everyone's very upset about it.
Somebody's been sleeping in my pod.
That'll be the lab hamster. It roams.
The lab hamster escaped again.
It's in the ceiling. It runs the ceiling now.
How long till we dock?
Three sunrises and a sandwich.
My cress grew sideways.
No gravity, no manners.
Is it cold, or is that the vacuum?
Thermostat. Deck nine runs chilly.
I dreamed I was on a planet.
Was it nice? Did things fall down?
Who rearranged the star charts?
Navigation. Says the stars moved first.
Fancy a game of floating darts?
Not after the incident. The vent has two.
The engines sound happy today.
Someone told them about the long weekend.
Do you ever miss weather?
I miss puddles. Never thought I'd say that.
What's the strangest thing in cargo?
A piano. Nobody admits to ordering it.
Is that rain on the window?
Ice crystals. Very glamorous ice crystals.
Have you tried the algae crisps?
Once. They tried me back.
Big asteroid on the scope earlier.
I waved. It didn't wave back. Rocks.
Who keeps adjusting the gravity?
The gravity tech. One per cent at a time.
Where's the best seat in the galley?
By the porthole. Bring a jumper.
Why do we have fire drills in space?
Because somebody brought a toaster.
The comms dish is pointing the wrong way.
It's sulking. It wanted the night shift.
Is this lunch or breakfast?
Sunrise says breakfast. My stomach says both.
Seen the aurora from up here?
Like curtains. Big green curtains.
I've lost my left glove.
Lost property has a system. It's a box.
Does anyone know how the lift works?
It doesn't work. It negotiates.
The new crew say the stars look fake.
They're real. They're just very tidy.
I fixed the porthole squeak.
Now the bulkhead squeaks. Out of jealousy.
Who's turned the hum up?
Nobody. That's the reactor on a good day.
Tea or coffee?
Whichever the recycler calls tea today.
Can we open a window?
Technically, once.
How's the backlog?
Strapped down and growing.
Is it Monday?
Calendar says day four hundred. So, yes.
I got a letter from my gran.
By shuttle? That's dedication.
The spacesuits smell of feet.
Feet and ambition.
What do you do on your rest day?
Float. Lie down. Float again.
Did you watch the launch replay?
I'm in it. I'm the one screaming.
Is the moon closer than yesterday?
We're closer. The moon stays put.
My mug won't stay put.
Strap it down. We strap everything down.
How cold is it outside?
Very. Don't check personally.
Anyone on the observation deck?
Two people and a very long sigh.
Is the soup meant to float?
Only if you let go of the lid.
We're passing the dark side soon.
It's not dark. It's moody.
The shuttle times changed again.
Shuttles are like comets. Late and shiny.
Did anyone feed the hydroponic fish?
They're fed. They're also suspicious.
What's that light out there?
A satellite. Or the window cleaner's torch.
A year on this ship today.
Happy launchiversary. Cake's in a tube.
How's the new console?
Lots of buttons. Three of them do anything.
Why is the corridor tilting?
It isn't. You've been in the gym.
Seen the captain's new chair?
It reclines. It's never been upright.
Is it true we're out of chocolate?
One bar left. It has a guard.
The hull's creaking again.
It's stretching. Long shift.
Is there a drill today?
There's always a drill. It's a ship.
Does the airlock ever feel lonely?
It has two doors. It's never alone.
I keep forgetting which way is down.
Down is wherever your lunch ends up.
Who designed these chairs?
Someone who'd never sat down, by the look.
Can you hear the stars?
No. That's the air scrubbers singing.
Busy on the bridge?
Lots of buttons. Lots of staring.
How's the cargo manifest?
Ninety crates. Plus my lunch.
Ever been out on a spacewalk?
Once. Lovely view. Itchy nose the whole time.
What do the cadets do all day?
Learn knots. Nobody knows why.
My pod alarm went off at four.
Four ship time is the best four.
Are we nearly there?
We're in orbit. We're always nearly there.
Is that new paint on deck six?
Hull grey. There were eleven greys.
Did the delivery drone come?
It came. It beeped. It left a note.
Why is everyone whispering?
Someone said 'hull breach' as a joke.
The galley's out of forks.
Spoons in space. Spoons for everything.
Fancy a jog round the ring?
I'll walk it. Backwards, for variety.
Did you hear about the micrometeorite?
Tiny thing. Big dent. Bigger paperwork.
Are the sleep pods getting smaller?
No. We're getting fond of pudding.
Is it sunrise again?
Seventh today. I've stopped saying morning.
Who's on comms tonight?
Night crew. And a very chatty satellite.
How do you water plants in zero g?
Gently. With a sponge and some hope.
Got a favourite constellation?
The one shaped like a sandwich.
I can't find the cargo bay.
Follow the cold. And the crates.
Ever think about how big space is?
Only when I drop a pen.
The grow lights are purple again.
The lettuces like it. It's their disco.
Did the captain say 'all hands'?
No, 'all snacks'. Different meeting.
What happens if the gravity fails?
Lunch gets very exciting.
Why does my console say 'nominal'?
It's an optimist. Like the rest of us.

staff.name: Priya Castellan
lines: Lettuces are thriving. I read them the news.
Please stop naming the tomatoes.
The basil leans to the porthole. It misses sun.

staff.name: Tomasz Wrona
lines: Tea round in five. Two hands on the mug.
A loose spoon was floating. It's in custody.
Kettle: four minutes. Queue: twelve.

staff.name: Devan Achari
lines: Undock it, redock it. Works nine times in ten.
Signal drops behind the moon. That's physics.
Label your cables. Space is big enough already.

staff.name: Nadia Oyelaran
lines: We pass the ocean at ten. Pick your window.
Sunrise every ninety minutes. Lunch at one.
The timetable is final, unless the planet moves.

staff.name: Augusto Pereira
lines: Gravity is set to one. Feel light? It's Friday.
Stop testing the gravity by jumping. It works.
Gravity down two per cent? Biscuits noticed.

staff.name: Bram Okafor
lines: The hold is strapped down. Even my lunch.
Borrowed a crate? Sign the form.
Stock take Thursday. Unhide the snacks.

staff.name: Yuki Ferrand
lines: This suit fits like a dream. A duvet dream.
Lost property: three gloves and a goldfish.
Breathe in. Zip's done. You may breathe out.

staff.name: Callum Navarro
lines: Best view on the ship, and I keep it clean.
Smudged stars are not my fault.
I wave at every shuttle. Half wave back.
